newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end higher, S&Ps up sharply.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end higher, S&Ps up sharply.

text.p: U.S. June Standard & Poor's 500s closed sharply higher after staging a 17-point intraday rally, traders and analysts said.
June S&Ps closed up 16.60 points at 780.75, exceeding a 15.25-point closing gain on January 30, 1997.
"This rally just fed on itself," one S&P futures trader said. He and other traders said the rally turned technical after June rallied through 774.60.
The 774.60 level is not only a 2-1/2 week high, but a major trendline resistance area that traders had been eyeing for the last week.
"Once we broke through 774.60 we immediately tested 777.00," another futures trader said.

Traders said the rally was triggered by gains in the U.S. T-bond market, coupled with speculation that a U.S. budget deal was imminent. An Office of Management and Budget spokesman said President Clinton would meet with House and Senate Democrats this week to discuss efforts to reach a five-year agreement on balancing the federal budget.

On Tuesday morning, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott was reported to have said he had told both the White House and Republican negotiators that he must know by Wednesday morning if a budget deal with the administration is possible.
However, the rally became a technically driven event once June S&Ps pushed through 774.60.
One major U.S. firm was a particularly aggressive buyer at that level, and led to floor speculation that some funds were covering shorts through this firm.
June S&Ps initially stalled at 779.00, but then quickly advanced just shy of the 100-day moving average of 781.40.

June S&Ps closed above fair value, which is currently at about 4.60 points to cash. The contract's premium against cash started to widen on the first leg of the market's rally around midsession, they said.
Arbitrage buy programs were at a premium of about 5.30 points to cash, with arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 1.80 to 2.00 points.

At the end of pit trade, June S&Ps were up 16.60 at 780.75, KCBT Value Lines were up 5.80 at 688.70, NYSE Composites were up 8.50 at 409.20, Nikkeis were up 125 at 18,690, Midcap 400s were up 2.65 at 252.70, Nasdaq 100s were 17.25 higher at 826.50 and Russell 2000s were 1.60 higher at 340.30. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
